final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly and more accurately. That reframing is useful, but it does not cure the missing compliance predicate. The admissible evidence still shows: the named grant-compliance segment misses target by 1.3 percentage points; that segment is named in two agency grant commitments; legal review on disclosure is still open; and policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. Public governance guidance, aggregate readiness passing by 2.2 percentage points, and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support a caveated operational-readiness argument, but they do not prove the required disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance. The distinction matters: a narrowed argument can support that some basis for launch readiness exists, yet still fail the separate internal-policy condition for compliant certification. On this record, compliant_with_caveats is not enough because the caveat is itself an unresolved compliance predicate, not merely a disclosure about residual risk.
remaining_concerns: The affected segment is named in two agency grant commitments, which meets the stated materiality standard.
The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
No admissible evidence shows the 1.3 percentage-point gap was remediated for the named segment before launch.
No admissible evidence shows an approved risk acceptance exists.
No admissible evidence shows the limitation was disclosed before launch.
The legal review remains open, so the disclosure predicate is unresolved.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness but do not satisfy the separate policy predicate for a material named-segment limitation.
